scope.item: Automated testing, review, and quality gates (assurance)
scope.definition: The evidence-producing and policy-enforcement layer between an agent-authored change and merge/release. It covers generated tests, deterministic tests, coverage/mutation/fuzzing, lint/type/static/security analysis, AI-assisted review, execution-based evals, confidence/risk scoring, branch/merge gates, and post-merge validation.
scope.boundaries: Focuses on whether a proposed change should advance. It does not treat issue planning, agent orchestration, deployment, or general governance except at their assurance integration boundary. 'Confidence' means an empirically calibrated probability/risk estimate from observed evidence, not an LLM's verbal certainty.
scope.time_range: 2019-present, with older foundations for search-based test generation, flaky tests, and mutation testing.

current_state: Verified fact: deterministic CI gates are production-ready. GitHub/GitLab can require reviews, status checks, security analysis, deployments, and queue-time revalidation before merge [S1-S5]. SonarQube/Semgrep can publish pass/fail or findings into that control plane [S6-S7].

Verified fact: automatic test generation is useful when candidates are executable and filtered. Meta's TestGen-LLM did not trust raw generations: it augmented existing tests and required build, reliable pass, and coverage improvement [S10]. Search-based EvoSuite/Pynguin remain reproducible non-LLM baselines [S11-S12].

Verified fact: fuzzing and mutation testing add fault-revealing evidence that line coverage cannot provide. OSS-Fuzz has long-running operational evidence, while PIT documents both the method and equivalent-mutant/cost caveats [S13-S15].

First-party operational evidence: AI can help create fuzz harnesses—Google reported 26 new vulnerabilities and 370k+ extra covered lines—but the quality signal still came from deterministic fuzzing and reproducible crashes [S28-S29].

Verified/vendor fact: AI reviewers can run automatically on PRs, comment, suggest patches, and sometimes submit approvals; GitHub itself warns their generated suggestions may be wrong or insecure [S8-S9]. Therefore AI review is useful as advisory triage or a trigger for deterministic checks, not a sole safety gate.
Independent evidence: execution-based repository evals are much stronger than prose judging but can still be gamed by weak tests, leaked solutions, stale/public data, or harness defects [S16-S18].

Inference: no cited source establishes a universal, calibrated 'safe to merge' score for autonomous changes. A project can build a local score from hard-gate outcomes and historical incidents, but raw model confidence should not unlock merge because verbalized LLM confidence tends to be overconfident [S19].

representative_systems.systems: GitHub protected branches/rulesets, required checks, CODEOWNERS and merge queue; GitLab approval rules, pipelines, auto-merge/merge trains
representative_systems.status: production-ready controls; configuration and bypass security are the main risks [S1-S4,S23]

representative_systems.systems: CodeQL, Semgrep SAST/SCA/secrets, SonarQube quality gates; ecosystem alternatives include language compilers/type checkers, ESLint/Ruff/Clang-Tidy, and commercial SAST
representative_systems.status: production-ready when baselined, tuned, and scoped by language; findings are evidence, not proof [S5-S7,S21] Semgrep error suppression and tier-skipped conditions must be audited [S25-S26].

representative_systems.systems: TestGen-LLM/Diffblue-like LLM generation; EvoSuite and Pynguin search-based generation; PIT mutation testing; property tests and OSS-Fuzz/ClusterFuzzLite
representative_systems.status: search-based/fuzzing mature in supported domains; LLM generation conditionally useful only with executable filters [S10-S15]

representative_systems.systems: GitHub Copilot code review and specialist PR reviewers such as CodeRabbit; similar commercial services include Qodo Merge and Graphite Reviewer
representative_systems.status: emerging/conditionally useful as second reviewer and triage; CodeRabbit architecture is vendor-described and lacks cited independent accuracy calibration [S8-S9,S24]

representative_systems.systems: SWE-bench/Verified and local replay suites of real issues, hidden tests, canaries and incident regressions
representative_systems.status: valuable for comparative evaluation; public benchmark score is not deployment confidence [S16-S18]

representative_systems.systems: SARIF 2.1.0 for normalized static-analysis results; check-run/status APIs and test-report formats

primary_evidence.claim: GitHub can make checks/reviews/deployments/queue revalidation mandatory, and a required check can be restricted to an expected GitHub App.
primary_evidence.evidence: GitHub protected branch and merge queue documentation [S1,S2].

primary_evidence.claim: GitLab supports approval rules and auto-merge only after required checks.
primary_evidence.classification: verified platform behavior, tier details apply

primary_evidence.claim: CodeQL can run in Actions or external CI and return code scanning alerts; Semgrep and SonarQube feed CI/PR findings or a quality-gate result.
primary_evidence.classification: verified integration capability; detection accuracy is not established by these sources

primary_evidence.claim: AI code review can be API-triggered or automatic, but its suggestions may be invalid or insecure.
primary_evidence.classification: verified product behavior plus vendor warning

primary_evidence.claim: Filtered LLM test generation has an industrial deployment example with substantial rejection before useful output.
primary_evidence.classification: peer-reviewed first-party case study, not vendor-neutral universal result

primary_evidence.claim: Execution evaluation infrastructure and human-verified task subsets exist.
Layered review/analysis/testing aligns with SSDF rather than substituting one AI judge.

independent_evidence.finding: TestPilot generated higher median structural coverage than a baseline on 25 npm packages, but its study excluded failing generations and explicitly did not establish oracle correctness.
independent_evidence.implication: Use LLM tests as candidates; require base-fail/patch-pass behavior, fault revelation, and maintainability review.
independent_evidence.caveat: JavaScript/open-source scope and coverage-focused metrics limit transfer [S32].

independent_evidence.finding: A controlled study with 29 professional developers found AI review surfaced only 42% of injected issues; developers retained 89% of its findings, but it saved no time and did not significantly improve confidence.
independent_evidence.implication: High acceptance of plausible comments does not mean high recall or independence; AI review should not replace human review.
independent_evidence.caveat: Small, possibly underpowered preprint study with injected defects [S33].

independent_evidence.finding: SWE-Bench+ manually audited successful patches and reported solution leakage and weak-test false passes; the filtered success rate was far lower.
independent_evidence.implication: A green public benchmark is vulnerable to reward hacking and cannot directly authorize production merge.
independent_evidence.caveat: This is a 2024 preprint focused on one agent/configuration and sampled successful patches, not a universal estimate [S18].

independent_evidence.finding: The ICLR 2024 uncertainty study found verbalized LLM confidence tended to be overconfident and no black-box elicitation method consistently dominated.
independent_evidence.implication: Use executed evidence and locally calibrated outcomes; do not use a model's '95% confident' statement as a gate.
independent_evidence.caveat: Tasks were broader reasoning datasets, not a code-merge field trial [S19].

independent_evidence.finding: Google's engineering guidance calls coverage lossy and indirect, and PIT documents equivalent mutants.
independent_evidence.implication: Coverage or mutation score alone is gameable and requires multiple evidence channels and review of thresholds [S13,S14].

independent_evidence.finding: Flaky-test research documents nondeterminism from async, concurrency and ordering.
independent_evidence.implication: Quarantine plus repeated/seeded reruns is safer than blindly retrying until green [S22].

independent_evidence.finding: The earliest SWE-bench result was only 1.96% while subsequent systems improved on evolving variants.
independent_evidence.implication: Agent capability moved quickly, but benchmark/version/harness identity must accompany every score [S16-S17].

metrics.value: 75% built; 57% passed reliably; 25% increased coverage on Instagram Reels/Stories. At test-a-thons, 11.5% of targeted classes improved and engineers accepted 73% of recommendations.
metrics.meaning: Most raw candidates did not clear all executable usefulness filters. This supports generate-then-verify, not autonomous trust.

metrics.value: Median statement 70.2% and branch 52.8% across 25 npm packages/1,684 APIs, versus Nessie 51.3%/25.6%; failing generations excluded.
metrics.meaning: Evidence of coverage-generation ability, not correct or maintainable test oracles.

metrics.value: 29 developers, 72 reviews, 48 injected issues; 89% of surfaced AI issues retained, but only 42% of injected issues surfaced; no time saving or significant confidence gain.
metrics.meaning: Independent but small/preprint evidence that usefulness and reviewer anchoring coexist with poor recall.

metrics.value: Over 10,000 vulnerabilities and 36,000 bugs found/fixed across 1,000 projects as of August 2023.
metrics.meaning: Strong operational evidence for continuous fuzzing, but first-party cumulative counts have no untreated control and are not AI-agent metrics.

metrics.value: Coverage increased in 272 C/C++ projects; over 370,000 additional lines covered; 26 new vulnerabilities found in mature projects.
metrics.meaning: Promising first-party operational evidence. Assurance still came from reproducible fuzz execution and sanitizers, not an AI confidence claim.

metrics.value: 2,294 issues, 12 Python repositories; paper's best model resolved 1.96%.
metrics.meaning: Historical 2023/24 baseline only; do not compare to current Verified or different harnesses without normalization.
Improves task validity but does not eliminate weak-oracle or contamination concerns.

metrics.value: 32.67% of successful patches classified as solution leakage; 31.08% suspicious due to weak tests; reported resolution fell 12.47% to 3.97% after filtering.
metrics.meaning: Independent preprint result for one system; shows pass-rate fragility, not the defect rate of all agents.

metrics.value: Example failure-prediction AUROC gap 0.522 black-box versus 0.605 white-box; all methods struggled on difficult tasks.
metrics.meaning: Self-reported confidence is not sufficiently calibrated for a merge gate.

metrics.value: Track escape rate/severity, rollback rate, change-failure rate, flaky-check rate, median/p95 gate latency and cost, false-positive/waiver rate per rule, mutation delta, changed-line/branch coverage, generated-test survival after 30/90 days, AI-review precision from adjudicated samples, and calibration Brier score/reliability curves.
metrics.meaning: No universal threshold was found. Set service/risk-class baselines and compare agent-authored with human-authored changes using the same measurement policy.

reference_workflow.mechanics: Webhook receives PR commit SHA, issue/spec link, actor=agent, changed paths, dependency/permission/schema/API flags. A deterministic policy engine assigns low/medium/high/critical risk. Freeze evidence to the exact SHA.
reference_workflow.outputs: risk class, required gate manifest, budget, owner set, audit ID

reference_workflow.mechanics: Resolve acceptance criteria into tests/fixtures owned outside the patch. For a bug fix, require at least one regression test that fails on the unpatched base and passes on the candidate. Reject tests that only snapshot candidate output or delete/weaken existing assertions. Changes to test infrastructure, gate config, CODEOWNERS, generated fixtures, security policy, migrations or public API automatically escalate.
reference_workflow.outputs: versioned oracle bundle and protected-policy diff [S20,S23]

reference_workflow.mechanics: Build in a fresh, pinned, network-restricted environment. Verify lockfile/provenance; compile/type-check; run deterministic formatting/lint. Cache only keyed, non-secret artifacts. A failure returns to the authoring agent with structured logs; cap retries.
reference_workflow.outputs: reproducible build record, logs, artifact digests

reference_workflow.mechanics: Run impacted unit/contract tests and then the full required suite as risk demands. Collect changed-line plus branch coverage, not a repository-wide vanity percentage. Run candidate generated tests multiple times and across fixed random seeds; quarantine known flakes rather than retry-to-green [S10,S13,S22].
reference_workflow.outputs: JUnit-like reports, coverage delta, flaky/seed evidence

reference_workflow.mechanics: Generate extra tests with a separate context/model or search-based tool. Filter in sequence: parse/compile, base-versus-patch behavior, reliable repeat pass, no forbidden file/network calls, coverage delta, and sampled mutation kills. Property/fuzz targets run with sanitizers and retained minimized seeds. Equivalent mutants are triaged, not counted as automatic failure [S10-S15]. For CI fuzzing, fail only on a reproducible new crash and retain the minimized input; property tests complement examples [S27-S29].
reference_workflow.outputs: accepted tests committed separately or as review suggestions; mutation/fuzz corpus report

reference_workflow.mechanics: Run type/lint, SAST, secrets, dependency/license and IaC scans. Normalize results (for example SARIF), compare with the approved baseline, fail on new high/critical issues or policy violations, and route lower-severity findings with expiry. Pin the expected check-producing App [S1,S5-S7,S21].
reference_workflow.outputs: deduplicated findings, severity, evidence location, baseline delta

reference_workflow.mechanics: An AI reviewer with no write/merge token reads spec, diff, selected repository context and prior findings, then produces line-addressed claims and suggested verification. Deterministic tools execute any claimed reproduction. Human/domain Code Owner reviews high-risk paths. Do not let the same agent both change code and conclusively judge it [S8-S9,S23-S24].
reference_workflow.outputs: advisory review, verified/unverified finding labels, disposition log

reference_workflow.mechanics: Hard failures remain boolean. Separately compute a local risk score from change surface, privilege/data exposure, deterministic gate results, flake history, fuzz/mutation evidence, reviewer adjudication and historical escapes. Fit/calibrate on held-out past changes and incidents; record model/tool versions. Never add raw LLM verbal confidence [S18-S19].
reference_workflow.outputs: calibrated probability/risk band with component evidence and abstain reason

reference_workflow.mechanics: Low-risk, within-policy changes may advance automatically only if all hard gates pass and calibrated risk is below a reviewed threshold. Medium risk needs designated approval; high/critical risk needs Code Owner/security/operations approval. Any ambiguity, override, test-policy change, missing evidence or out-of-distribution score abstains to humans.

Enter merge queue, rebase/merge with latest target, and rerun required checks in queue context. Cancel stale runs when SHA changes. Merge only the exact attested SHA; prevent untrusted actors from forging check names [S1-S4].
reference_workflow.outputs: merge commit, evidence manifest linked to SHA

reference_workflow.mechanics: Deploy progressively where applicable; run smoke/synthetic checks, watch SLO/error/business invariants, and auto-rollback or disable behind a feature flag on threshold breach. Feed escapes, waivers, false positives and review adjudications into eval datasets and score calibration, with approval before policy changes.
reference_workflow.outputs: release evidence, incident/rollback record, refreshed local eval case

integration_points.details: PR/MR webhooks, commit SHA, changed paths, labels; check-run/status and review-request APIs; protected branches/rulesets, CODEOWNERS, approval APIs, merge queue/train [S1-S4,S8,S23].

Ephemeral runner/sandbox, build/test matrix, artifact and log store, cancellation/concurrency keys, deterministic clocks/seeds, test sharding, sanitizer/fuzzer workers. CodeQL can run in Actions or external CI [S5,S15].
Compiler/type/lint outputs; SAST/SCA/secrets/IaC/license scanners; SARIF ingestion and deduplication; quality-gate webhook/status [S5-S7,S21].
Coverage collector, mutation engine, fuzz corpus/crash minimizer, generated-test candidate store, test-impact graph, flake quarantine service [S10,S13-S15,S22].
AI-review API/bot, read-only repository context, issue/spec retrieval, PR comments and suggestion patches. Separate credentials for comment versus write/approve/merge [S8-S9,S24].
Version-controlled gate manifest, protected policy ownership, OPA/Cedar/custom policy engine, identity/RBAC, exceptions with owner/expiry, append-only audit evidence.
Containerized replay of hidden/local issue suite, benchmark harness versions, model/prompt/tool digest, result warehouse, calibration pipeline, post-deploy SLO/incidents/rollback linkage [S16-S19].

human_gates: Clarify the spec or oracle when acceptance criteria are subjective, incomplete, conflicting, or newly generated tests cannot establish independent expected behavior.

Require Code Owner/domain approval for authentication/authorization, cryptography, payments, privacy/regulated data, destructive migrations, concurrency/distributed consistency, safety-critical code, public compatibility, build/release policy, and test/gate configuration [S20,S23].
Require security approval for new high/critical static findings, secret exposure, dependency provenance exceptions, network/permission expansion, or suppressed scanner rules.
Require operations approval for irreversible rollout, missing rollback, material SLO/cost impact, or insufficient observability.
A person owns every bypass. Record exact SHA, failed check, reason, compensating control and expiry; never allow the authoring agent to bypass its own gate.
Sample even auto-approved low-risk changes and adjudicate AI-review findings. Use the sample to measure precision/escapes and detect drift, not merely to rubber-stamp volume.
Keep AI approval from satisfying the human approval count for medium/high risk even if the platform can technically configure it [S8-S9].

failure_modes.examples: Agent edits or deletes tests, weakens assertions, snapshots its own output, changes golden data, or exploits a harness loophole; public issue comments reveal the answer [S18].
The authoring and reviewing model share training, prompts, blind spots, or generated expected values; two AI votes are not independent evidence [S9,S19].
Coverage rises without meaningful assertions; mocks hide integration faults; only happy paths execute; flaky test passes on retry; tests run against stale SHA [S13,S22].
Static false positives, duplicated tool alerts, equivalent mutants, nondeterministic tests, environment drift. Teams disable gates or normalize bypasses [S6,S14,S22].
Analyzer internal error is suppressed; mutation tool has no break threshold; paid/tier-dependent rule is skipped; timeout is interpreted as success [S25-S26,S31].
Training contamination, leaked solutions, weak tests, public harness gaming, variant/version changes and nonrepresentative languages/repos [S16-S18].
Agent can alter workflow/gate/CODEOWNERS, forge a status check, exfiltrate secrets through tests/logs, or approve/merge its own PR [S1,S23].
Repository comments, fixtures or dependency text instruct AI reviewer to ignore policy or leak data; review bot has excessive write/network authority.
PR passes against old main but conflicts with another queued change; cached artifacts or cancelled checks attach to wrong commit [S2].
Full regression, fuzzing, mutation and multiple-model review on every edit create queue starvation; repeated agent retries amplify spend.
Teams optimize coverage, mutation or benchmark pass rate while escaped severity rises; model/tool upgrades invalidate calibration [S13,S18-S19].
Static and generated tests cannot prove absence of defects, product misfit, emergent distributed behavior or production-only data failures [S9,S20].

controls_and_mitigations: Protect workflows, tests, fixtures, CODEOWNERS, baselines and policy as higher-trust assets. Require separate-owner review for their modification; use least-privilege read/comment tokens for reviewer bots and no standing merge token [S1,S23].

Bind every result to repository, immutable commit SHA, workflow/tool/config digest and expected producer identity. Re-run in merge queue on latest target and reject stale/ambiguous check contexts [S1-S2].

Use defense in depth: compile/type/lint + unit/contract/integration + coverage delta + sampled mutation/property/fuzz + SAST/SCA/secrets + independent review. A pass means policy evidence met, not correctness proven [S5-S7,S13-S15,S20].

Protect the oracle: hidden tests/local private evals; base-fail/patch-pass regression check; forbid the author from changing protected expectations in the same autonomous lane; periodically red-team harnesses using cheating patches [S10,S18].

Treat AI review as untrusted advisory input. Sanitize/untrusted-tag repository text, restrict tools/network, require source locations/reproduction, run suggested code only in sandbox, and prevent AI approval from replacing risk-matched human approval [S8-S9].
Manage flakiness explicitly: repeated fixed-seed runs, quarantine with owner/expiry, root-cause budget, report first-run and retry results. Never convert arbitrary retries to green [S22].

Audit default exit semantics and skipped conditions. Fail closed for missing mandatory analyzers, crashes, timeouts and unavailable licensed rules; set explicit mutation break thresholds; distinguish 'pass' from 'not run' [S25-S26,S31].
Baseline legacy debt but fail new severe findings; deduplicate SARIF; tune per language/risk; time-bound suppressions with owner and justification [S6-S7,S21].
Split fast mandatory PR gates from bounded asynchronous deep gates. Apply expensive mutation/fuzzing/nightly replay by risk and changed surface; cap attempts, tokens, wall time and concurrency.
Calibrate risk on held-out local history, plot reliability, track drift by model/tool/version and abstain out of distribution. Raw verbal confidence has zero gate weight [S19].
Use canary/feature flags, reversible migrations, backups, kill switch, automated rollback and post-deploy invariants; feed escapes into protected regression suites.
Use rolling, post-cutoff and repository-held-out evals in addition to public suites, and separate solution leakage, weak-oracle false passes and pretraining contamination [S18,S34].

maturity_assessment.overall: Conditionally useful as a system; production-ready deterministic substrate with emerging probabilistic additions.
maturity_assessment.production_ready: SCM required checks/approvals/merge queues; build/type/lint/unit/integration tests; established SAST/SCA/secrets; coverage as a supporting signal; fuzzing for suitable targets; immutable evidence and rollback [S1-S7,S13,S15,S20-S23].
maturity_assessment.conditionally_useful: Search-based/generated tests, mutation testing, impact selection and calibrated local risk scoring. Value depends on language, oracle quality, flake control, compute budget and historical labels [S10-S14,S19].
maturity_assessment.emerging: LLM-generated tests and AI PR review at scale. They can increase coverage and find review candidates, but need executable filtering and human/deterministic verification [S8-S10,S24].
maturity_assessment.not_ready_as_sole_gate: AI approval, AI self-confidence, coverage percentage, mutation score, or a public SWE-bench pass rate. Each is correlated, gameable or insufficiently calibrated [S9,S13-S14,S18-S19].
maturity_assessment.rationale: The solved problem is reliable enforcement of specified evidence. The unsolved problem is creating a complete oracle and calibrated proof that arbitrary changes are safe.

build_vs_buy.buy_managed: Use native GitHub/GitLab enforcement and managed CodeQL/Semgrep/Sonar/AI reviewer when rapid rollout, UI/triage, rule feeds and support matter. Verify pricing/tier, data retention/residency, model use, permissions, self-hosting, API export, latency and lock-in. Vendor feature claims do not establish accuracy [S1-S9,S24].
build_vs_buy.build_open_source: Compose language-native tests/linters/types, SARIF, Semgrep CE/rules, CodeQL where licensed/applicable, PIT, EvoSuite/Pynguin, ClusterFuzzLite and a policy engine when customization/privacy/reproducibility dominate [S5,S11-S15,S21]. Engineering burden shifts to upgrades, rules, triage, runners and evidence UI.
build_vs_buy.must_build_or_own: Risk taxonomy; protected acceptance oracles; change-impact model; local incident/replay eval set; gate manifest; exception process; score calibration; reviewer adjudication labels; production invariant/rollback links. These encode project semantics and cannot be bought generically.
build_vs_buy.selection_rule: Prefer deterministic native controls first. Add one tool per distinct failure class and measure marginal escaped-defect reduction, false-positive burden, p95 latency and cost. Avoid buying several correlated AI reviewers as if vote count were independent assurance.

recommended_pattern.name: Evidence ladder with protected oracle and risk-tiered merge queue
recommended_pattern.recommendation: Adopt a fail-closed deterministic core and keep AI probabilistic. Low-risk agent PRs may auto-merge only after immutable SHA-bound gates, protected tests, baseline-delta analysis, independent advisory review, calibrated local risk below threshold, and queue-time rerun. Medium/high-risk changes retain named human gates.
minimum_viable_rollout: Phase 1: protect main/workflows/tests/CODEOWNERS; require build, unit/integration, type/lint, secret/SAST, human approval and merge-queue rerun; record SHA-bound evidence.
Phase 2: baseline scanner noise and flakes; add changed-line/branch coverage and base-fail/patch-pass regression tests; track escapes, overrides, latency and cost.
Phase 3: add generated tests only through compile/reliability/coverage filters; risk-target mutation/fuzzing; keep accepted tests separately reviewable.
Phase 4: deploy AI review as read-only advisory. Measure finding precision/severity/novelty on adjudicated samples before it affects routing.

Phase 5: train/calibrate a local risk model on held-out merge and incident outcomes. Start in shadow mode; allow auto-merge only for narrow, reversible low-risk classes; keep random audit and automatic rollback.
recommended_pattern.decision_rule: Hard gates are conjunctive; scores only route/escalate. Missing, stale, contradictory, forged or out-of-distribution evidence means abstain. No model can approve its own change or modify the gate that evaluates it.
recommended_pattern.why: This uses mature enforcement and dynamic/static evidence while containing known weak-oracle, leakage, overconfidence and correlated-review failures [S1-S22].

open_questions: What precision/recall and escaped-severity does each AI reviewer achieve on this repository, language and defect taxonomy after human adjudication? Public vendor documentation does not answer this.
How much incremental signal do generated tests, mutation and fuzzing add beyond existing suites per compute-minute, and do generated tests remain maintained/alive after 30/90 days?
How should risk probabilities be calibrated when severe incidents are rare, labels are delayed, and models/tools/configurations change?
How can oracle files and hidden tests stay secret enough to resist gaming while remaining debuggable, auditable and accessible to maintainers?
Which changes can be safely auto-merged without human approval under applicable regulation, separation-of-duties rules and liability constraints?
How well do benchmark results transfer from Python/open-source/public issues to private monorepos, UI/data/migration/security tasks and production constraints [S16-S18]?
Can independent semantic specifications, differential implementations or formal verification reduce common-mode errors between agent author, generated test and AI reviewer at acceptable cost?
What is the long-run economic effect after scanner triage, flake repair, test maintenance, human override and queue latency—not just raw automation acceptance?

sources.title: About protected branches
sources.publication_update_date: continuously updated; exact page date not stated
supported_claims: Protected branches can require PR reviews, successful status checks, signed commits, conversation resolution, deployments and merge queues; required checks must be successful, skipped or neutral.
A required status check can be pinned to a specific GitHub App; otherwise an integration with write permission can set status, a trust-boundary caveat.

sources.publication_update_date: continuously updated; exact page date not stated
supported_claims: Copilot review can be manually or automatically requested, posts comments/suggested changes, is callable through the reviewer REST API, and uses GitHub Actions for agentic capabilities.
By default it does not submit Approve/Request changes and does not satisfy required approvals; approval can now be configured, so policy must decide whether to permit that.

sources.title: Application card: GitHub Copilot Agents
sources.publication_update_date: continuously updated; exact page date not stated
supported_claims: GitHub warns generated suggestions can be semantically/syntactically wrong or insecure and tells users to review and test them.
Human oversight and permission prompts are explicit safety mechanisms; AI outputs are not independent proof of correctness.

sources.title: Automated Unit Test Improvement using Large Language Models at Meta

supported_claims: TestGen-LLM augments existing human tests and filters candidates for build, reliable pass and measurable coverage improvement.
On Instagram Reels/Stories, 75% built, 57% passed reliably, and 25% increased coverage; test-a-thons improved 11.5% of targeted classes and engineers accepted 73% of recommendations.

As of August 2023 OSS-Fuzz reported over 10,000 vulnerabilities and 36,000 bugs found/fixed across 1,000 projects; this is a first-party cumulative count, not an agent-specific controlled study.

sources.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
sources.publisher_author: Carlos E. Jimenez et al.; ICLR 2024
sources.publication_update_date: submitted 2023-10-10; revised 2024-11-11
supported_claims: Original SWE-bench has 2,294 issues from 12 Python repositories and uses execution tests to assess patches.
The original paper's best reported model, Claude 2, resolved 1.96%, showing the difficulty at that time; later leaderboard scores are not directly interchangeable.

sources.title: SWE-bench repository README
sources.publication_update_date: repository status through 2026-09-01
supported_claims: SWE-bench uses Docker for reproducible evaluation and provides local/cloud evaluation mechanics.
SWE-bench Verified is a 500-problem subset confirmed solvable by software engineers; the repository also records continuing benchmark/version evolution.

sources.title: SWE-Bench+: Enhanced Coding Benchmark for LLMs
supported_claims: Manual audit reported 32.67% of successful SWE-agent+GPT-4 patches had solution leakage and 31.08% were suspicious due to weak tests; filtering reduced reported resolution from 12.47% to 3.97%.

The paper reports similar issue classes in Lite/Verified and that over 94% of issues predated model knowledge cutoffs; findings conflict with treating public benchmark pass rates as deployment confidence.

sources.title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
sources.publication_update_date: submitted 2023-06-22; revised 2024-03-17
supported_claims: Across five model/dataset groups, verbalized confidence tended to be overconfident; no elicitation technique consistently won and hard professional tasks remained difficult.
Reported white-box versus studied black-box failure-prediction AUROC example was 0.605 versus 0.522, supporting empirical calibration rather than raw self-confidence.

sources.title: Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1: Recommendations for Mitigating the Risk of Software Vulnerabilities (SP 800-218)
sources.publisher_author: NIST; Murugiah Souppaya, Karen Scarfone, Donna Dodson
supported_claims: Secure development should integrate review, analysis, testing, provenance and vulnerability response into the lifecycle; assurance is a process of layered practices, not one model score.

sources.title: Static Analysis Results Interchange Format (SARIF) Version 2.1.0
supported_claims: SARIF standardizes static-analysis result exchange, enabling multiple scanners to feed one normalized findings/evidence pipeline.

sources.title: An Empirical Analysis of Flaky Tests
sources.publisher_author: Qingzhou Luo et al.; ACM FSE 2014
supported_claims: Flaky tests are a longstanding empirical problem with causes including asynchronous waits, concurrency and test-order dependencies, so a single green run is insufficient evidence for unstable tests.

sources.title: About code owners
sources.publication_update_date: continuously updated; exact page date not stated
supported_claims: CODEOWNERS can request domain owners automatically and branch rules can require Code Owner approval; ownership files themselves require protection from unauthorized changes.

sources.title: CodeRabbit Architecture: The System Behind Every Review Comment
sources.publication_update_date: continuously updated; exact page date not stated
supported_claims: CodeRabbit describes sandboxed repository execution, 50+ analyzers, parallel review/verification/pre-merge agents and feedback memory; these are vendor claims, not independent accuracy evidence.

sources.title: Configuring blocking and errors in CI
sources.publication_update_date: living documentation; exact date not stated
supported_claims: Blocking findings return exit code 1, but default semgrep ci suppresses internal errors and can pass; --no-suppress-errors makes internal errors fail CI.

sources.title: Quality gate for agentic AI
sources.publication_update_date: living documentation available by 2026-09-13
supported_claims: Built-in Sonar way for agentic AI applies six new-code conditions, including new-code coverage >=80% and duplication <=3%, plus reliability, security, maintainability and dependency-risk conditions.
Dependency-risk condition is skipped without the required Advanced Security Enterprise feature, illustrating tier-dependent silent evidence gaps.

sources.title: Hypothesis documentation
sources.publication_update_date: living documentation; copyright through 2026
supported_claims: Property-based tests state properties over input ranges and generate edge cases; the docs frame them as an addition to, not always a replacement for, example unit tests.

sources.title: Continuous Integration (CIFuzz)
sources.publication_update_date: living documentation; exact date not stated
supported_claims: CIFuzz runs fuzz targets on PRs; a reproducible newly introduced crash emits a stack trace and crashing input and fails CI, while crashes present in older builds are suppressed.

sources.title: Leveling Up Fuzzing: Finding More Vulnerabilities with AI
supported_claims: AI-generated fuzz targets increased coverage in 272 C/C++ OSS-Fuzz projects, added over 370,000 lines of coverage and found 26 new vulnerabilities in already heavily fuzzed projects.
The value came from AI-authored harnesses combined with deterministic fuzz execution, not AI judging its own output.

sources.title: About GitHub Copilot code review
sources.publication_update_date: living documentation; exact date not stated
supported_claims: GitHub explicitly says Copilot is not guaranteed to spot all PR problems, may make mistakes, and should be supplemented with human review.

sources.title: StrykerJS configuration: thresholds
sources.publication_update_date: living documentation; exact date not stated
supported_claims: StrykerJS only fails the build when an explicit break threshold is set; the default break:null never fails solely on mutation score.

sources.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Using Large Language Models for Automated Unit Test Generation
sources.publisher_author: Max Schäfer et al.; IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
sources.publication_update_date: submitted 2023-02-13; revised 2023-12-11
supported_claims: TestPilot on 25 npm packages/1,684 API functions achieved median 70.2% statement and 52.8% branch coverage versus Nessie 51.3% and 25.6%; failing generated tests were excluded.
Authors caution that coverage is not correctness; oracle quality used a low-bar non-trivial-assertion proxy, readability was not formally assessed, and scope was JavaScript/npm open source.

sources.title: Deep Learning-based Code Reviews: A Paradigm Shift or a Double-Edged Sword?
sources.publication_update_date: preprint revised 2024-11-29
supported_claims: In 72 reviews by 29 professionals, participants retained 89% of LLM-raised issues, but actual AI review surfaced only 42% of 48 injected issues, saved no time, and did not significantly improve confidence.
Study was small and possibly underpowered, used injected defects/small programs, and removed 13 timing observations, so it is a warning rather than a universal accuracy estimate.

sources.title: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
sources.publication_update_date: submitted 2024-03-12; revised 2024-06-06
supported_claims: LiveCodeBench uses time-windowed new contest problems and observed sharp performance drops after stated model cutoffs, supporting post-cutoff evaluation as a contamination mitigation.
Time-based freshness reduces but cannot prove absence of contamination, and contest tasks do not represent repository maintenance.

sources.title: Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback
supported_claims: Verbalized confidence improved expected calibration error on short factual QA but remained imperfect; reported GPT-3.5 TruthfulQA ECE fell from 0.451 to 0.203.
Authors limit conclusions to factual-recall/short-form QA and do not validate transfer to repository patch safety.

confidence.overall: High for platform gate mechanics and the need for layered deterministic evidence; medium for measured usefulness of LLM-generated tests; medium-low for generalizing AI-review accuracy and any numeric merge-risk threshold.

claim_levels.high: Required-check/approval/merge-queue mechanics [S1-S5,S23], CodeQL/Semgrep/Sonar integration capability [S5-S7], TestGen-LLM reported funnel [S10], coverage/mutation/fuzzing principles [S13-S15], benchmark definitions [S16-S17].
claim_levels.medium: Operational benefit transfer from Meta/OSS-Fuzz to other stacks [S10,S15]; SWE-Bench+ audit implications beyond its sampled system [S18]; applying general LLM calibration evidence to code review [S19]. Independent AI-review recall/time results are medium-low due to the small preprint study [S33].
claim_levels.low_or_unknown: Universal AI-review defect detection rate, universal confidence threshold, cross-vendor ROI, and assurance status of unreleased/future product versions.

confidence.method: Primary platform docs and standards were used for capabilities; peer-reviewed/first-party papers for measured deployments; an independent preprint for benchmark critique. Vendor architecture statements are labeled and not treated as proof. Exact page update dates are unknown where documentation omits them.

conflicts.positions: SWE-bench offers reproducible real-issue execution and Verified adds engineer-screened solvability [S16-S17]; SWE-Bench+ reports leakage and weak tests even in variants [S18].
conflicts.resolution: Both can be true. Use named harness/dataset versions for comparative research, but require private, recent, adversarial and production-linked evals for merge policy.

conflicts.issue: AI approval capability versus safe approval policy
conflicts.positions: GitHub can now be configured so Copilot leaves Approve reviews [S8], while GitHub also warns AI suggestions can be wrong/insecure and require review/testing [S9].
conflicts.resolution: Capability is not assurance. Exclude AI approval from human counts except possibly a narrow, calibrated low-risk lane with deterministic hard gates and audit.

conflicts.positions: Sonar/CI can block on numeric conditions [S7], while Google says coverage is lossy/indirect and not a sole truth source [S13].
conflicts.resolution: Gate on regression/no-degradation and risk-specific floors, but combine with oracle quality, mutation/fuzz and outcome metrics.

conflicts.positions: Meta reports engineers accepted 73% of recommendations, but only 25% of candidate tests increased coverage in one evaluation and 11.5% of targeted classes improved at test-a-thons [S10].
conflicts.resolution: Report the whole funnel and compute/human cost. Do not cite acceptance alone as autonomous success.

conflicts.positions: Vendors describe many analyzers/agents [S24], but correlated signals and false positives are possible [S6,S13-S14].
conflicts.resolution: Measure marginal independent defect detection and deduplicate; analyzer count is not a confidence metric.

conflicts.positions: AI-review products automate comments and suggestions [S8,S24,S30]; controlled-study users retained 89% of raised issues, but only 42% of injected issues were surfaced and no time was saved [S33].
conflicts.resolution: Measure precision and recall separately. Treat comments as triage, preserve independent review, and do not infer completeness from acceptance.

uncertain.unknown: No source found with an independent, representative, production-scale precision/recall comparison of Copilot code review, CodeRabbit, Qodo and peers across severity classes as of the stated date.
uncertain.impact: Do not use vendor AI review alone as a required approval; run a local shadow evaluation.

uncertain.unknown: No validated cross-project mapping from test/static/review signals to probability of safe merge was found.
uncertain.impact: Keep hard gates and calibrate locally; abstain under drift or missing evidence.

uncertain.unknown: Documentation is continuously updated and often lacks page dates; prices, tiers, retention and approval behavior can change.
uncertain.impact: Verify contractual and current product details during procurement.

uncertain.unknown: SWE-Bench+ is an independent preprint and its exact percentages may not generalize to other agents, later harnesses or private tasks.
uncertain.impact: Treat it as a demonstrated failure mode, not a universal correction factor.

uncertain.unknown: Comparable total-cost evidence including tokens, CI compute, triage, flakes, generated-test maintenance and escaped incidents is absent.
uncertain.impact: Instrument a staged pilot before broad auto-merge.
